title: Harmonize transitive deps across Python/JS/Go clients and add CI benchmark gates
creator: Ravi Patel
description:
Background: Over the last two quarters we observed multiple small but correlated regressions in p95 token latency for hosted API calls originating from client libraries (Python, JS and Go). Root cause analysis shows a combination of divergent transitive dependency versions (http clients, connection pools, JSON libraries), a couple of accidental polyfilled shims in the JS bundles, and a missed upgrade of the Go http2 transport that reduced effective concurrency.

Proposal: Coordinate a semver-safe bump strategy for top-level and transitive deps across the three language clients, pin a minimal compat matrix, and add CI benchmark gates so future bumps cannot be merged without passing latency/regression checks. Key actions: 
1) Audit transitive dependency trees for each client and identify variance windows where multiple versions are being pulled in (e.g., requests/urllib3 mismatches in Python; node-fetch vs undici; Go: net/http2 vendor differences).
2) Define a small shared compatibility matrix (library + allowed semver ranges) and add it to SDK contributing docs.
3) Make targeted changes rather than all-in upgrades: bump connection-pool and transport-related deps first, then work through JSON/parsing and telemetry libs.
4) Add microbenchmark harnesses in CI that run a short canonical request pattern against a local mock runtime and assert no >5% increase in p95 token latency and no >10% increase in median token CPU.
5) Add e2e smoke on latest Node LTS and newest stable Python/Go release in the SDK release pipeline.

Acceptance criteria: 
- All three clients have dependency manifests updated and lockfiles regenerated with proof of deterministic installs (sha sums).
- CI includes a regression benchmark job that fails the PR if latency regression thresholds are exceeded.
- Documentation updated with compatibility matrix and upgrade policy.
- No customer-facing API surface changes; deprecated parameters removed after compatibility period and feature flags if needed.

Risks & Mitigations: 
- Risk: A transitive bump could change serialization behavior. Mitigation: Add unit tests for request serialization and round-trip contract tests against the mock runtime.
- Risk: Flaky CI benchmarks due to noisy host. Mitigation: Run benchmarks on a small pool of pinned runners and aggregate results across 3 runs; use median.

Notes: This is intentionally conservative (no mass major-version bumps). The goal is to remove the small multi-lang drift that is contributing to latency and unpredictable tail behavior, and to stop regressions from being merged unnoticed.
comments: 2025-01-16 - Initial audit: Ran 'pipdeptree' on current wheel CI artifact, 'npm ls' on the JS package, and 'go mod graph' for Go. Found three hotspots: python urllib3 (1.25.x vs 1.26.x), JS fetch shims (node-fetch still referenced by a transpile-only devDep in bundler config), Go: x/net/http2 indirect pinned to an older commit in one internal tool. Collected lockfile diffs into a quick artifact: https://drive.redwood/example-dep-audit

2025-01-20 - Decision: Follow semver-minor-first path. Bumped Python urllib3 to 1.26.x across packages and regenerated poetry.lock; update validated locally against mock runtime. Marisol opened PR #4582 (https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk/pull/4582).

2025-01-24 - CI benchmark harness prototype merged into dev branch. Harness runs a canonical 256-token generation against mock-runtime with 1k request burst (simulated). Initial numbers: baseline p95=82ms, post-bump p95=88ms (7% regression) — exceeded threshold. Investigating hotspot: telemetry flush interval in Python client introduced extra blocking I/O in background thread. Created a follow-up ENG-914205 to refactor telemetry flush non-blocking path.

2025-01-28 - Trade-off: Reverted an aggressive JSON parser upgrade in JS after noticing 10% increase in median CPU. Instead, patched bundler to remove dev-only shims and switched to undici runtime for Node LTS tests. JS PR #4620 updated bundler config and reduced bundle size by 22%.

2025-02-02 - Current status: Python urllib3 change landed behind a feature flag and is running canary for internal smoke tests. Go transport bump is staged but blocked on an internal test harness fix (ENG-914210). Benchmark CI job added to branch protection with three-run median aggregation. Next: finish telemetry non-blocking refactor and schedule a cross-team review with runtime team to verify kernel selection sensitivity.
Reviewer notes: Please pay attention to the benchmark noise section in the PRs; if you see p95 flicker by more than 2% across runs, add a test runner tag so we can exclude bad hosts.
